planting.note: Direct sow after last frost; Magellan stays notably compact and sturdy compared to most large-flowered zinnias, making it a good choice for beds and containers where taller cut-flower zinnias would flop.

directions: Direct sow into well-drained soil in full sun after the danger of frost has passed. Magellan is an All-America Selections winner bred for large, fully double, dahlia-like flowers on unusually compact, sturdy plants, giving the visual impact of a tall cut-flower zinnia on a dwarf, well-branched habit that rarely needs staking. It blooms in a wide range of colors from cream and yellow through orange, salmon, pink, and deep red, flowering heavily from midsummer to frost with regular deadheading. Its compact size and strong garden performance make it well suited to bedding, borders, and containers, and good air circulation between plants helps reduce the powdery mildew that affects zinnias in humid climates.

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost; Isabellina shares the same tall, sturdy, long-stemmed habit as its Queeny Lime series relatives and is grown mainly as a cut flower for its unusual soft coloring.

directions: Sow seed a quarter inch deep after last frost in full sun and thin to 12-18 inches. Isabellina produces large, semi-double to double blooms in a soft, muted butter-yellow that ages toward cream, a subtle coloring prized by cut-flower growers for blending into pastel and neutral-toned bouquets alongside the similarly muted Queeny Lime series. Plants are tall and vigorous with strong stems well suited to cutting, blooming from midsummer through frost with regular harvesting or deadheading to keep new flowers coming. Grow in full sun with good air circulation to reduce powdery mildew, the main disease risk for zinnias in humid climates, and stake in windy sites since the large flower heads can be top-heavy on tall stems.
